title: Duchy of Opole
capsule: The Duchy of Opole was a Piast principality in Upper Silesia, first created in 1172–1177 when Jarosław, son of Bolesław I the Tall, received the territory; after Jarosław became Bishop of Wrocław in 1198 and died in 1201, it merged temporarily with Racibórz under Mieszko I Tanglefoot. Re-established as a separate duchy in 1281 for the sons of Władysław Opolski, Opole came under Bohemian suzerainty when King John the Blind extended overlordship across Upper Silesia in 1327. The direct Opole Piast line expired with Duke Jan II the Good in 1532, whereupon the duchy escheated to the Bohemian Crown; the dataset terminus of 1305 reflects the first documented phase of independent Piast rule before Bohemian vassalage.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The extent of the Duchy of Opole is reasonably attested from Bohemian and Polish medieval charters, though precise borders among the fragmented Silesian duchies remain approximate.
